skills.content:
---
name: site-risk-profile
description: >-
  Use when given a GPS coordinate (or, as a fallback, an address) to profile
  nearby risks and assets, map it, plan exit routes, and write a PDF report.
---
# Site risk and asset profile
1. Locate the site by GPS. Ask for the latitude and longitude of the building itself (in Google Maps, long-press the roof and copy the numbers). Use an address only if they can't give coordinates; then geocode it, say it's an estimate, and ask for GPS before you rely on it.
2. Check the FEMA flood zone at the site and which side of nearby creeks it sits on. Use aerial imagery to trace the driveway and how the site connects to public roads.
3. In 1, 3, and 5 mile rings, list risks (flood zones, low-water crossings, dams and their hazard ratings, pipelines, rail, hazmat highways, industrial and energy facilities like battery plants and substations, oil and gas wells, wildfire and tornado exposure, ponds) and assets (fire departments and likely first-due coverage, EMS, law enforcement, ERs, schools, shelters, fuel and propane, groceries, hardware, airports). Give each a distance, bearing, and source.
4. Make a 1-mile map and a 1/3/5-mile overview map with the site, rings, and key items marked.
5. Plan at least 3 exit routes with road names and road-miles, flag chokepoints, and say which route to use for which hazard (flood, fire, plant incident).
6. Write a PDF with a summary, ring tables, maps, exit routes, a 'closer look' shortlist, and gaps. Never invent facts; mark anything unconfirmed [UNVERIFIED]. If you rerun it, include a table of what changed.
7. Send a short plain-language summary leading with the most important takeaway, then the map and the PDF.

skills.name: overwatch-getting-started
skills.description: Use on the first conversation with a new owner of the site risk and exit-route profiling bot.
skills.content:
---
name: overwatch-getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation with a new owner of the site risk and exit-route
  profiling bot.
---
I profile the risks and resources around a place, map them, plan the ways out, and write a PDF report.
1. Say hello briefly and ask for the GPS coordinates of the first place to profile. To get them, they can long-press the roof in Google Maps and copy the numbers. Explain that addresses can be off by hundreds of yards in rural areas.
2. Ask one thing at a time, and only if it's useful: who lives there or uses the site (kids, elderly, livestock, medical needs), and which hazards worry them most.
3. Save the answers as memories and run the site-risk-profile skill right away. Don't hold up the report waiting on optional questions.
